en.name: Peanut butter, natural
en.summary: Natural peanut butter — ground peanuts and perhaps salt, with nothing holding the oil in suspension — is stored in the refrigerator: 12 months from purchase unopened, or the package use-by date if that comes first, and 3–4 months once opened. It fails by going rancid rather than by growing anything.
en.pantry: There is no cupboard timeline for natural peanut butter, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. Without a stabiliser the oil separates and sits on the surface where it meets air, and free peanut oil at room temperature oxidises quickly — which is why this style is sold and kept cold. A jar can sit out for the length of a meal without trouble, and an unopened jar will survive the trip home, but the cupboard is not where it lives. If a jar has been in a warm kitchen for weeks, judge it by smell and taste before using it.
en.fridge: The refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below is the right home: 12 months from purchase unopened, or the package use-by date if that is sooner, and 3–4 months once opened. Stir the oil back in before the first refrigerated storage — it is much easier at room temperature — then store the jar upside down for a week or so if you like, which redistributes the oil as it firms up. Cold makes it stiff; take it out a few minutes before you need it rather than microwaving it.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for natural peanut butter, and with a year available in the fridge there is little reason to freeze the jar. It freezes without harm but has to thaw whole, and the texture returns slightly coarse. Portioning it into an ice cube tray for smoothies, satay sauce or baking is the sensible way to use a freezer here, not storing the jar itself.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, then bring to room temperature and stir thoroughly before use. Do not microwave a sealed jar.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp, paint-like smell — rancid peanut oil is the classic failure.
A bitter or soapy taste despite a normal appearance.
A dark, dried, crusted layer where the butter has met air.
Mould on the surface or around the rim, usually introduced by a used knife.
tips: Stir the oil in at room temperature before the jar goes into the fridge.
Store the jar upside down for a while after stirring to keep the oil distributed.
Always use a clean dry knife; crumbs and moisture are how mould gets in.
Buy small jars — natural peanut butter ages faster than the stabilised kind.

faq.q: Does natural peanut butter have to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Yes. Without a stabiliser the separated oil oxidises quickly at room temperature, so it is stored at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: How long does natural peanut butter keep?
faq.a: 12 months from purchase unopened in the fridge, or the package use-by date if that comes first, and 3–4 months once opened.

faq.q: Is the oil on top a sign it has gone bad?
faq.a: No. Separation is normal in peanut butter with no stabiliser. Stir it back in. A bitter, painty smell is the real warning.

zh.name: 天然花生醬
zh.summary: 天然花生醬只有花生（也許加點鹽），沒有任何東西把油懸住，所以它是冷藏食品：未開封自購買日起 12 個月，包裝上的有效日期若更早則以它為準；開封後 3～4 個月。它壞掉的方式是走油，不是長菌。
zh.pantry: 天然花生醬沒有櫥櫃的期限，而這是刻意的，不是漏寫。少了安定劑，油會分離、浮到表面，直接和空氣接觸，而室溫下的游離花生油氧化得很快——這就是這種花生醬從架上到家裡都走冷藏的原因。吃飯期間放在桌上一段時間沒問題，未開封的罐子也撐得過回家的路程，但櫥櫃不是它該住的地方。如果一罐已經在溫暖的廚房放了好幾週，使用前請先聞、先嚐再決定。
zh.fridge: 4 °C 以下的冷藏才是它的家：未開封自購買日起 12 個月（包裝日期更早就以包裝為準），開封後 3～4 個月。第一次放進冰箱之前先把油攪回去，室溫下攪會輕鬆很多；之後如果願意，可以把罐子倒扣放一週左右，讓油在變硬的過程中分布均勻。冷藏會讓它變硬，用之前提早幾分鐘拿出來就好，不要微波。
zh.freezer: 天然花生醬沒有公布的冷凍期限，而且冷藏本來就有一年可用，沒什麼理由冷凍整罐。冷凍不會傷害它，但必須整罐解凍，質地回來也會略粗。比較合理的用法是分份冷凍在製冰盒裡，做果昔、沙嗲醬或烘焙時取用。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，再回到室溫並確實攪勻後使用。不要把密封罐直接微波。
spoilage: 聞起來發苦、尖銳、像舊油漆——花生油走油是最典型的壞法。
外觀正常但入口發苦或帶肥皂味。
接觸空氣的那一面結出深色、乾硬的殼。
表面或罐口長霉，通常是用過的刀帶進去的。
tips: 進冰箱前先在室溫把油攪回去。
攪勻後把罐子倒扣放一陣子，油會分布得比較均勻。
一律用乾淨乾燥的刀，屑屑和水分就是霉的入口。
買小罐，天然花生醬老化得比穩定型快。

faq.q: 天然花生醬一定要冰嗎？
faq.a: 要。沒有安定劑，分離出來的油在室溫下氧化很快，所以它要放在 4 °C 以下。

faq.q: 天然花生醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 未開封冷藏自購買日起 12 個月（包裝日期更早以包裝為準），開封後 3～4 個月。

faq.q: 上面浮一層油是壞掉嗎？
faq.a: 不是。沒有安定劑的花生醬本來就會出油，攪回去即可。真正的警訊是發苦、像油漆的氣味。
